- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.2) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect momentum decay.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation; increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 periods to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the 10-15 day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply a +3% bias to forecast for 10-15 day window if sentiment swings > 0.5 in last 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 to -1.2 to +0.5), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1-2 days ahead of true trend, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome in 30-day window, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, add a +2-5% bias to forecast for next 10-15 days to account for sentiment-driven mean reversion.
